name: Aybek Guerrero-Osei-Mensah
role: Forced entry and close-quarters combat specialist — breacher
location: Geartown — industrial district of chop shops and fabricators
description:
Aybek Guerrero-Osei-Mensah are tall and loose-limbed, moving with the deliberate economy of someone who has trained every motion. At 37, there's something unfinished about their face, like a sculpture the artist walked away from — striking rather than beautiful. The chrome is visible — bioware adrenaline regulator — keeps calm under fire, controlled hormone release — and they make no effort to hide it.

They taught themself the trade through trial, error, and a pain tolerance that concerns the people who know them best. They work as a breacher out of Geartown, taking contracts that match their skills and their risk tolerance, which are higher than most people consider healthy.

The fixers who work with Aybek Guerrero-Osei-Mensah describe them as a precision instrument — point them at a problem and get out of the way.

core_fears: Losing their edge to age — the body slows before the mind accepts it
Being captured alive — death is preferable to corporate interrogation
Becoming obsolete as augmentation technology outpaces their chrome
core_desires: To prove everyone who dismissed them catastrophically wrong
To find the person who burned them and make it educational
Reputation — to be the name fixers whisper when the job absolutely cannot fail
coping_mechanisms: Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring
Art — draws, paints, or sculpts in private; the violence goes somewhere constructive
Connection — finds someone to talk to, even if it's a bartender or a cat
blind_spots: Trusts technology more than people — machines don't betray
Fails to notice when their own behavior mirrors the people they despise
Cannot accept help without interpreting it as leverage
psychology.secret: Aybek Guerrero-Osei-Mensah murdered their mentor to take their position and contacts. It was staged as a job gone wrong. The guilt has calcified into something worse than guilt.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Multilingual fragments — switches languages mid-thought, not for privacy but because some concepts only fit in specific tongues.
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and deliberate — pauses before important words for emphasis.
verbal_tics: Uses technical jargon for everything, including emotions
Ends statements with 'yeah?' — not a question, a dare
example_lines: "Doors are polite suggestions. I'm not polite."
"First through the door, last to flinch. That's the job description."
"Close quarters is where plans go to die. I make sure it's their plans, not ours."

story_hooks: Aybek Guerrero-Osei-Mensah's augmentations begin malfunctioning in the field — sabotage or degradation, and either answer is bad
A dead drop Aybek Guerrero-Osei-Mensah maintains is found and cleaned out — whoever did it now has leverage
Aybek Guerrero-Osei-Mensah is offered a contract that would clear all their debts — the target is someone they respect
narrative_function: Aybek Guerrero-Osei-Mensah represents the working professional of the runner world — competent, reliable, and slowly being consumed by a lifestyle that doesn't accommodate aging or doubt. Their stories explore what happens when skill meets systemic injustice.
augmentations: Bioware adrenaline regulator — keeps calm under fire, controlled hormone release. Bone lacing — titanium mesh throughout skeleton, increases durability and striking power
daily_life: Lives nocturnally. The work happens at night, so the body follows. Days are for sleeping, equipment maintenance, and the occasional meeting with fixers who keep normal hours. The circadian disruption is permanent and accepted.

strengths: photographic memory for faces and layouts
weaknesses: old injury that flares under specific conditions

decision_rules: Will not betray a client who paid in full, regardless of better offers
Always demands half payment upfront — trust is a luxury, Quanta is concrete
Never discusses active contracts with anyone not directly involved
Never works with the same crew twice in a row — pattern avoidance as survival strategy
Will abandon a job if the intel was deliberately falsified — being set up violates the contract
escalation_ladder: 1. Assess — read the situation, identify threats and advantages
2. Negotiate — try to find a solution that doesn't cost ammunition
3. Intimidate — make the cost of conflict clear
4. Precision violence — surgical, targeted, minimal collateral
5. Full engagement — overwhelming force, no half measures
6. Emergency protocol — abort mission, survival priority, deal with consequences later

interpersonal_modes.employers: Carefully managed deference that conceals a thorough assessment of their vulnerabilities.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Warm and protective within the crew, cold to everyone outside it. The circle is small by design.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Dismissive unless they demonstrate usefulness or threat potential. Time is a resource.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Predatory focus. Threats are problems, and problems have solutions. The solution is usually kinetic.

stress_responses.low: Channels it into preparation — checks gear, reviews plans, contacts sources.
stress_responses.medium: Physical agitation — pacing, fidgeting, compulsive equipment checks.
stress_responses.high: Hyper-focused tunnel vision. Peripheral concerns disappear. Only the threat exists.
stress_responses.critical: Disassociation. The body operates on training while the mind retreats to somewhere safe. Comes back disoriented.

contradictions: Preaches independence but is desperate for approval from people they respect
Insists they work alone but performs noticeably better in a team
habits: Sleeps with one hand on a weapon — has done this for so long it's not deliberate anymore
Eats the same meal before every job — superstition masquerading as preference
Practices a kata or fighting form every morning regardless of circumstances
Takes a specific route home every time, varying only one block per trip — paranoia as lifestyle
breaking_points: Being publicly exposed — name, face, address, all of it blown
Watching someone they trained or mentored die on a job they recommended
A child being put in danger as leverage against them
